answer.generated: Concurrency control mechanisms, such as locks, play a crucial role in ensuring data integrity during concurrent transactions within a file-processing system. Locks are designed to manage access to shared resources by coordinating between multiple transactions to prevent conflicts. In a file-processing system, locks can be implemented using various types such as exclusive (X) and shared (S) locks to control access rights and prevent deadlocks. By carefully managing these locks, the system ensures that each transaction either completes successfully or rolls back if it violates the consistency rules, thereby maintaining data integrity even under concurrent operations.
